basic_information.name: Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
basic_information.creator: Linux Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI
basic_information.license: Apache 2.0 (all hosted projects use OSI-approved open source licenses; the three founding projects — MCP, goose, AGENTS.md — are all Apache 2.0)
basic_information.current_version: N/A — AAIF is a governance foundation, not a software release; individual projects maintain their own versioning (MCP spec 2025-11-25, goose 100+ releases, AGENTS.md v1)

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: N/A — AAIF is a standards body and governance foundation, not a software framework. It hosts three distinct projects: MCP (protocol, client-server architecture), goose (single_agent, local-first), and AGENTS.md (convention/standard, file-based).
technical_architecture.underlying_models: AAIF itself is model-agnostic. Its hosted projects support all major LLMs: MCP works with any LLM through client implementations; goose supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and open-source models via API; AGENTS.md is model-independent (read by any coding agent).
technical_architecture.tool_integration: MCP is the primary tool integration standard hosted by AAIF. MCP defines a universal protocol for connecting AI models to tools, data sources, and applications using a JSON-RPC-based client-server architecture. The ecosystem has grown to 3,000+ MCP servers covering developer tools (GitHub, VS Code, Docker), productivity suites (Google Drive, Asana, Slack), databases, and cloud services. goose uses MCP natively as its tool integration layer.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: N/A — AAIF as a foundation does not prescribe planning approaches. Individual projects vary: goose uses LLM-driven planning with code execution capabilities; MCP and AGENTS.md are infrastructure-level standards that agents of any planning approach can use.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: AAIF standards are designed to enable multi-agent interoperability. MCP provides the shared protocol layer that allows multiple agents to connect to the same tools and data sources. AGENTS.md provides shared project-level instructions readable by any agent. goose itself is primarily a single-agent framework but can interact with other agents via MCP. The foundation's broader mission is to ensure agents from different vendors can collaborate through shared open standards.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: N/A — AAIF is a governance body. Memory is handled at the project level: MCP defines Resources (for exposing data) and context management primitives; goose manages conversation context with local-first persistence; AGENTS.md provides static project-level context (procedural/semantic knowledge encoded in markdown files).
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Not directly managed by AAIF. MCP addresses context by providing a standardized way for AI systems to access external data (Resources) and execute tools (Tools), reducing what needs to be in the context window. AGENTS.md uses hierarchical file discovery (nearest file in directory tree takes precedence) to provide relevant project context without overwhelming the agent.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: Varies by project: MCP is a stateless protocol (persistence is implementation-dependent); goose uses local file system persistence; AGENTS.md is file_system-based (markdown files committed to repositories).
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: AAIF's approach to context is architectural: MCP treats context as a first-class concern by providing a universal protocol for agents to discover and access relevant data sources, tools, and resources. AGENTS.md treats project context as a first-class concern by providing a standardized, machine-readable location for operational instructions that coding agents need. Together, they form a layered context engineering stack: AGENTS.md for project-level instructions, MCP for tool/data access, and individual agent implementations for conversation-level context.

capabilities.core_capabilities: AAIF provides neutral governance, open standard development, and community coordination for the agentic AI ecosystem. Its three founding projects deliver complementary capabilities: (1) MCP — universal protocol for connecting AI agents to external tools, data sources, and applications; defines primitives for Tools (executable functions), Resources (data exposure), and Prompts (reusable templates); enables any AI client to connect to any MCP-compatible server. (2) goose — open source local-first AI agent that can build projects from scratch, write/execute code, debug failures, run tests, install dependencies, orchestrate multi-step workflows, and interact with external APIs autonomously; works with any LLM via API. (3) AGENTS.md — standardized markdown convention for providing AI coding agents with project-specific guidance including setup commands, testing workflows, coding style preferences, architecture overviews, security policies, and PR guidelines; adopted by 60,000+ open source projects. AAIF also hosts events (MCP Dev Summit), maintains a landscape project, and coordinates interoperability standards development across the industry.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Varies by project: MCP supports text, code, and structured data exchange (modality-agnostic protocol); goose supports text, code, file system, browser, and command-line interactions; AGENTS.md supports text/markdown.
capabilities.autonomy_level: N/A for AAIF as a governance body. goose operates at fully_autonomous level (executes code, runs commands without per-step approval). AGENTS.md and MCP are infrastructure standards used by agents at any autonomy level.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: The MCP ecosystem (governed by AAIF) has expanded to 3,000+ servers. Categories include: developer tools (GitHub, VS Code, Docker, JetBrains), productivity (Google Drive, Asana, Slack, Notion), databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Elasticsearch), cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), security tools, monitoring systems, and more. goose can connect to any MCP server via its plug-and-play architecture. The ecosystem is growing rapidly with new servers contributed by the community and member organizations.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: MCP is one of AAIF's three founding projects. AAIF provides neutral governance for the MCP specification, SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Kotlin, Java, C#, Swift, Go), and ecosystem. MCP is the primary interoperability standard hosted by the foundation.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol by Google) is not currently an AAIF project. However, AAIF's open governance model allows new projects to be proposed and accepted based on demonstrated adoption, quality, and community health. MCP and A2A are complementary protocols (MCP for tool integration, A2A for agent-to-agent communication).
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: AGENTS.md is one of AAIF's three founding projects. Originally created by OpenAI and collaborators (Amp, Cursor, Factory, Google Jules), it is now stewarded by AAIF under the Linux Foundation. Adopted by 60,000+ repositories and supported by all major coding agents including Codex, Cursor, Devin, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Jules, VS Code, and Claude Code.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Cross-framework compatibility is AAIF's core mission. The foundation exists specifically to ensure agents from different vendors and frameworks can interoperate through shared open standards. MCP provides framework-agnostic tool integration (any agent framework can implement an MCP client). AGENTS.md provides framework-agnostic project instructions (any coding agent can read the files). goose serves as a reference implementation showing how these standards work together. The stated goal is to become 'what the W3C is for the Web' — ensuring interoperability, open access, and freedom of choice across the agentic AI ecosystem.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: AAIF does not prescribe a specific permission model but promotes safety patterns as part of its standards work. MCP includes authorization specifications (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, Resource Indicators for preventing token misuse). goose runs locally with user-level permissions. The foundation is working on production-grade security profiles for MCP servers and certified MCP server vetting processes as near-term milestones.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Not standardized at the AAIF level. Individual projects implement their own: goose supports human-in-the-loop patterns; AGENTS.md can encode escalation rules in project instructions; MCP delegates authorization to server implementations. The foundation's safety working groups are expected to develop recommendations.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Not directly addressed by AAIF governance. However, the standards help indirectly: MCP provides verifiable tool execution (agents can check real data rather than hallucinate); AGENTS.md provides ground-truth project context reducing agent confusion; goose's local-first approach means agents can verify against actual codebases and test results.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: MCP supports tracing and logging at the protocol level. goose logs agent actions locally. AGENTS.md changes are tracked via version control (git). AAIF's governance decisions are public and transparent. The foundation is expected to develop audit trail recommendations for production agentic systems.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: AAIF promotes human oversight as a design principle but does not mandate a specific pattern. The standards enable various patterns: MCP's authorization model supports pre-approval for sensitive operations; AGENTS.md can encode review requirements and approval workflows; goose supports interactive and autonomous modes. The foundation's safety work is expected to formalize oversight recommendations.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: AAIF is itself the governance body, operating as a directed fund under the Linux Foundation. It is governed by a Governing Board composed of member representatives (Platinum members get board seats). Technical Steering Committees (TSCs) manage individual projects. The Linux Foundation provides operational infrastructure and expertise in neutral open-source governance.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: AAIF governs and advances three founding protocols/standards: (1) Model Context Protocol (MCP) — the universal protocol for AI-to-tool integration; (2) AGENTS.md — the open standard for project-level agent instructions; (3) goose — the reference open-source agent framework implementing MCP. The foundation is open to accepting additional projects that meet criteria of demonstrated adoption, quality, community health, and OSI-approved licensing.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: AAIF does not directly certify compliance but its open, transparent governance model supports regulatory alignment. The foundation's interoperability standards help enterprises implement auditable, standardized agent infrastructure. MCP's authorization framework supports enterprise security requirements. The open-source nature of all projects supports transparency requirements under regulations like the EU AI Act. No specific SOC2, HIPAA, or EU AI Act certifications are claimed at the foundation level.

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: N/A for AAIF as a governance body. For its projects: MCP is protocol-level (deployed wherever agents and servers run — cloud, local, hybrid, edge); goose is primarily local-first (desktop app + CLI) but can be deployed in cloud and enterprise environments; AGENTS.md is file_system-based (deployed in any code repository).
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: N/A for AAIF governance. MCP is a protocol enabling horizontal scalability (unlimited servers, unlimited clients). goose is designed for individual developer use but enterprise deployment patterns are under development. AGENTS.md scales with repository count (no infrastructure needed).
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: AAIF membership fees: Platinum $350,000/year, Gold $200,000/year, Silver $10,000/year. All hosted projects are free and open source — no per-task costs from the foundation. Operational costs are determined by the LLM APIs and infrastructure used by individual agent deployments. goose is free to use with any LLM API (costs determined by the LLM provider chosen).
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: N/A for AAIF governance. MCP servers are lightweight (Node.js or Python processes). goose requires a modern desktop/laptop with internet access for LLM API calls. AGENTS.md requires no infrastructure (markdown files in git repos).

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: AAIF member Datadog is a Gold member, suggesting monitoring integration is a priority. MCP supports standard observability patterns. goose provides local logging and execution traces. The foundation is expected to develop observability recommendations for production agent deployments. No AAIF-specific monitoring tool exists yet.
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: MCP includes protocol-level support for tracing agent-tool interactions. goose logs execution traces locally. AGENTS.md changes are traced via git history. Member companies like Datadog and Chronosphere (Silver member) bring observability expertise to the foundation.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: AAIF as an organization: early-stage (founded December 2025, ~2 months old). MCP: production_ready (used by major enterprises, deployed on AWS, GCP, Azure). goose: beta (27K+ GitHub stars, 350+ contributors, but still rapidly evolving). AGENTS.md: production_ready (adopted by 60,000+ projects). The foundation's governance structures are still being established.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: AAIF organization on GitHub: 1 repository (AAIF landscape) with 26 stars. Individual project stats: MCP spec repo 7.1K stars, MCP Python SDK 21.6K stars, MCP TypeScript SDK 12K stars; goose (block/goose) 27K+ stars; AGENTS.md (agentsmd/agents.md) — stats not separately tracked but adopted by 60,000+ repos.
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: 49 member organizations across three tiers (8 Platinum, 18 Gold, 23+ Silver, growing). MCP ecosystem: 3,000+ servers, used by all major cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) and coding tools (Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot). goose: 27K+ GitHub stars, 350+ contributors, 100+ releases. AGENTS.md: adopted by 60,000+ open source projects and all major coding agents. The broader agentic AI market is projected to grow from $7.8B to $52B by 2030 (Gartner predicts 40% of enterprise apps will embed AI agents by end of 2026).
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: AAIF membership is fee-based (Platinum: $350K, Gold: $200K, Silver: $10K per year). All hosted projects are free and open-source. The foundation follows the Linux Foundation's proven directed fund model. No per-use or per-agent fees exist for the standards and protocols.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Enterprise AI agent interoperability and standardization; developer tooling integration via MCP (connecting AI coding agents to IDEs, version control, CI/CD, databases); autonomous software development workflows (goose for local-first coding); project-level agent governance (AGENTS.md for consistent agent behavior across repositories); secure agentic infrastructure for regulated industries; startup ecosystem building (lowering integration costs via shared standards).
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: AAIF is the first and currently dominant standards body specifically for agentic AI. It occupies a unique position as a neutral governance home for the de facto standards in the space (MCP has become the industry standard for agent-tool integration). Comparison: Google's A2A protocol is not yet part of AAIF (but Google is a Platinum member). No competing foundation exists with comparable industry backing. The closest analogs are W3C (for web standards) and the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (for cloud infrastructure). AAIF's main risk is fragmentation if key protocols remain outside the foundation.

ecosystem_maturity.community_size: 49+ member organizations including 8 of the world's largest tech companies. Individual project communities: MCP has 187+ contributors on the spec repo alone, with thousands more building MCP servers; goose has 350+ contributors; AGENTS.md is adopted by 60,000+ projects. The foundation hosts the MCP Dev Summit (next: NYC, April 2-3, 2026). The broader community includes developers at all member companies plus independent open-source contributors. Airbyte and other organizations continue to join (as recently as January 2026).
ecosystem_maturity.documentation_quality: good — MCP has comprehensive documentation at modelcontextprotocol.io (specification, guides, SDKs, examples). goose has documentation at block.github.io/goose. AGENTS.md has documentation at agents.md. AAIF's own website (aaif.io) covers membership, news, and projects. Documentation is still evolving given the foundation's youth (2 months old).
ecosystem_maturity.third_party_integrations_count: 3,000+ MCP servers in the ecosystem (the primary integration surface). Major platform integrations include AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, Microsoft Azure, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, JetBrains, Docker, and many more.
ecosystem_maturity.tutorial_availability: Moderate. MCP has official quickstart guides, SDK tutorials, and server development documentation. goose has getting-started guides and Docker integration tutorials. AGENTS.md has usage guides from OpenAI and community blog posts. Multiple third-party tutorials, blog posts, and conference talks exist. The MCP Dev Summit provides in-person learning opportunities. Official AAIF learning resources are still being developed.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: N/A for AAIF as a foundation. The standards it governs support the full spectrum: AGENTS.md can encode instructions for any autonomy level; MCP enables tool access at any level from copilot to fully_delegated; goose operates primarily as autonomous (acts independently to complete tasks) but supports interactive modes.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Not standardized by AAIF. Individual implementations vary: MCP supports authorization-based handoffs (sensitive operations require human approval); goose supports interactive mode where users guide the agent; AGENTS.md can encode handoff rules (e.g., 'always request review for security changes'). Standardizing handoff patterns is a likely future workstream for the foundation.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Not yet standardized by AAIF. At the project level: goose supports iterative feedback through conversation; AGENTS.md can be updated based on observed agent behavior; MCP servers can be refined based on usage patterns. The foundation's open governance model means feedback from member organizations and the broader community shapes project direction through TSCs, issues, and pull requests.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: AAIF is critically important for startup founders building in the agentic AI space. Key considerations: (1) Build on AAIF standards (MCP, AGENTS.md) to ensure interoperability with the broader ecosystem — this is becoming table stakes, not optional. (2) MCP compliance means your AI tools/services can be discovered and used by any MCP-compatible agent, massively expanding your addressable market. (3) Silver membership costs only $10K/year and provides networking, visibility, and input into standards that will shape the industry. (4) The open-source nature of all projects means zero licensing costs for using the protocols. (5) For startups building agent frameworks: differentiate on UX, domain expertise, or safety — not on proprietary protocols (MCP is winning the protocol war). (6) For startups building SaaS: expose your API as an MCP server to be instantly usable by any AI agent. (7) Risk: if you build on proprietary agent protocols, you risk being locked out as the industry standardizes around AAIF-governed standards. (8) Timing: the market is early (foundation is 2 months old) — now is the time to contribute to standards and build on them before they ossify.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: For AAIF standards adoption: always adopt (free, open-source, industry-standard). The real build-vs-buy question is whether to join AAIF as a member. Silver membership ($10K) is worthwhile for startups seeking influence and visibility in the agentic AI ecosystem. For building agent capabilities: use goose or similar frameworks as a starting point, contribute MCP servers for your domain, and add AGENTS.md to your repositories. Do not try to build competing standards — the industry has coalesced around MCP. Instead, invest in domain-specific value on top of these open standards.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 1 (Fundamentals & AI landscape — understanding the agentic AI ecosystem and key players), Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — understanding open standards, Build vs Buy for agent infrastructure), Session 5 (Ethics, governance & final presentations — open source governance, industry coordination, EU AI Act alignment)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official Linux Foundation press releases, member company announcements (OpenAI, Block, Anthropic, Cisco), TechCrunch, InfoQ, SiliconANGLE, and the official aaif.io website. Foundation is very recent (Dec 2025) so information is current but the organization is still establishing itself.
confidence.cross_reference: Multiple authoritative sources confirm all key facts: Linux Foundation press release, OpenAI blog post, Block blog post, TechCrunch reporting, InfoQ analysis, SiliconANGLE coverage, PYMNTS analysis, CIO Dive, Medium critiques, and official GitHub repositories for MCP (7.1K stars spec, 21.6K Python SDK), goose (27K+ stars), and AGENTS.md (60K+ adoptions).
confidence.caveats: AAIF is extremely new (founded December 9, 2025 — only 2 months old at time of writing). Governance structures are still being established. The foundation has not yet accepted projects beyond the three founding ones. Membership fees have drawn criticism (Platinum $350K paywall for board seats). The relationship between AAIF and Google's A2A protocol is unclear (Google is a Platinum member but A2A is not yet contributed). Technical Steering Committees are still forming. The long-term sustainability and neutrality of the foundation will depend on execution over the coming years. Some critics argue the contributions are peripheral tools rather than core competitive assets. The 60,000+ AGENTS.md adoption figure and 3,000+ MCP server count are rapidly evolving and may be outdated quickly.
